8821185.title: Dungka!
8821185.extract:
# Dungka!
Dungka! (stylized in all caps as DUNGKA!) is a song by the Filipino boy band SB19. It was released on April 25, 2025, as part of their third extended play (EP) Simula at Wakas, under Sony Music Philippines. Musically, "Dungka!" is an energetic pop track incorporating rave and hyper-pop elements. Its lyrics deliver a defiant message to critics and naysayers, with the title derived from the Filipino phrase “doon ka” meaning “go over there” or colloquially “go away”. Upon release, the song gained significant attention for its vibrant music video showcasing Filipino street culture and for achieving strong chart performance.
## Background and release
SB19 announced Simula at Wakas as the final installment of a trilogy of EPs that began with Pagsibol (2021) and Pagtatag! (2023). Ahead of the EP’s release, the group released the single “DAM” in February 2025 as a comeback track. Simula at Wakas (which translates to "Beginning and End") was then released on April 25, 2025, including "Dungka!" as one of its focal tracks. All five members of SB19 took a hands-on role in the EP’s creation, with member John Paulo Nase (known as Pablo) leading the songwriting and co-producing tracks alongside his brother Josue under their production moniker RadKidz.
"Dungka!" was not pre-released as a standalone single but was highlighted upon the EP’s launch with a music video on the same day. In interviews, SB19 described the EP as a celebration of their journey and evolution. Within that context, “Dungka!” serves as a bold statement track, thanking supporters and pushing back against detractors. The song’s title is a play on a common Filipino expression “doon ka”, meaning “go there,” which the band uses as a tongue-in-cheek way to tell detractors to step aside.
## Composition and lyrics
"Dungka!" is an upbeat P-pop song that blends multiple genres. Critics have noted its “maximalist” production, filled with electronic rave-style beats and even hyperpop influences. The track features rap verses delivered by members Pablo and Josh, as well as powerful group vocals, over a pounding dance rhythm. The production is characterized by heavy bass and synth layers, giving it an intense, high-energy sound. The song was produced by SB19’s Pablo and Josue (RadKidz), who infused it with experimental sounds while keeping a pop structure.
Lyrically, "Dungka!" is often described as SB19’s clapback at negativity and online criticism. The lyrics address social media bashers, “crab mentality” (a local term for pulling others down), and judgmental stereotypes in a confrontational yet witty manner. The hook centers on the phrase “dungka!”, a slang contraction of “doon ka,” meaning “go over there.” This phrase is repeated as a refrain telling off naysayers to basically “go away”. Despite its aggressive premise, SB19 delivers the message in a playful tone. Reviewer accounts note that the song manages to be empowering and fun at the same time, turning a dismissive phrase into a celebratory anthem of self-confidence. By using everyday colloquial language and cultural references, the track remains authentic to Filipino listeners while being accessible to new audiences. SB19 has mentioned that “Dungka!” reflects their refusal to be dragged down by criticism, aligning with the EP’s broader themes of perseverance and renewal.
## Music video
The music video for "Dungka!" premiered on April 25, 2025, coinciding with the EP release. Running nearly six minutes long, the video is a vibrant montage that pays homage to Filipino street life and culture. It depicts the members of SB19 performing in lively community settings: neighborhood basketball courts, streets lined with food vendors, and local block parties. Scenes in the video showcase everyday activities and iconic Filipino pastimes – for example, men playing street basketball, groups doing Zumba dance exercises in a parking lot, kids hopping through 10-20 (a traditional Filipino jump-rope game), people singing karaoke, and vendors selling street foods like fishballs and kwek-kwek. In the background, there are also visuals of political rally posters and a mock election campaign, adding a touch of social commentary to the festive atmosphere.
A notable aspect of the "Dungka!" video is its many cameo appearances by well-known Filipino personalities. SB19 enlisted a star-studded lineup of guest cameos to embody various facets of Filipino pop culture. Appearances include YouTube gamer Ghost Wrecker, comedian and TV host Vice Ganda, cosplay celebrity Alodia Gosiengfiao, TikTok comedian Sassa Gurl, and social media star Mimiyuuuh. The video also features rappers Smugglaz and Shehyee, online entertainers Kween Yasmin and Malupiton, as well as Pat Lasaten and Agnes Reoma (members of the OPM band Ben&Ben), among others. Each cameo guest is integrated into the scenes—such as Vice Ganda dramatically arriving in a neighborhood scene—to amplify the song’s message of pride and solidarity in Filipino identity.
Throughout the video, SB19 and the cast joyously perform and interact with the community around them. The visual narrative subtly responds to the song’s themes: for instance, one comedic scene shows a character (portrayed by Ghost Wrecker) literally devouring a crab, a tongue-in-cheek reference to “crab mentality”. Other scenes address gender stereotypes and social biases in a humorous way, reinforcing the song’s stance against judgment and prejudice. The overall tone of the "Dungka!" music video is celebratory and defiant. Critics praised its authentic portrayal of Filipino everyday life, noting that it feels “stubbornly, brilliantly local” while delivering a universally relatable message of resilience.
## Reception
Upon release, "Dungka!" received a positive reception from both fans and music critics. Commentators highlighted it as one of the standout tracks on Simula at Wakas, applauding SB19’s bold creative choices. Bandwagon Asia described the song as “one of the biggest surprises of the EP” for its daring sound and maximalist production style. The Southeast Asian culture magazine VMAN similarly complimented "Dungka!" as a "joyful portrait of Filipino life" and noted that it refuses to dilute its local flavor, effectively turning a very Filipino experience into something with broad appeal. The music video in particular was widely acclaimed for its cultural richness and the playful inclusion of celebrity cameos. Philippine media outlets like GMA News and the Philippine Daily Inquirer remarked on the video’s celebration of Filipino culture and community spirit. Fans on social media also embraced the song’s message, often quoting the titular catchphrase “Dungka!” as a rallying cry against negativity.
In terms of commercial performance, "Dungka!" achieved notable chart success for a Filipino release. In May 2025, it debuted on the Billboard Philippines Hot 100 at number 21, marking SB19’s latest entry on their home country’s main chart. Internationally, the song also made an impact: "Dungka!" entered the U.S. Billboard World Digital Song Sales chart at number 7. This debut gave SB19 another top-ten hit on that global digital sales chart, underlining the group’s growing international fanbase.
The track’s popularity was further cemented by industry accolades. In October 2025, "Dungka!" won Pop Song of the Year at the inaugural Filipino Music Awards. This award, presented by an organization affiliated with Billboard Philippines and other media, recognized "Dungka!" as the year’s top pop song in the Philippines, with SB19 beating fellow nominees including Sarah Geronimo and BGYO. The song was also honored as Song of the Year at the 2025 PPOP Music Awards, a ceremony celebrating Pinoy pop acts, highlighting how strongly "Dungka!" resonated within the P-pop community. These achievements reflect the song’s wide appeal and the impact it had in 2025 as an empowering anthem.
By the end of 2025, "Dungka!" had become one of SB19’s signature tracks. Its blend of modern pop bravado, Filipino cultural elements, and an empowering message helped solidify SB19’s reputation as trailblazers in contemporary Pinoy pop music. The phrase “Dungka,” once a regional slang, entered the broader vernacular of fans as a memorable slogan symbolizing SB19’s triumphant stance against detractors.

SB19's 'DUNGKA!' music video features cameos from Vice Ganda, Sassa Gurl, Pat and Agnes, and more!
==================================================================================================

By GMA Integrated News

**Published** April 25, 2025 3:40pm  

SB19 pulled out all the stops for their music video for “DUNGKA!”

The [P-Pop Kings](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/tracking/sb19/) showcased Filipino culture in the almost six-minute MV, with activities like street basketball, Zumba, fliptop, activism, election campaigns, street food, 10-20, karaoke, and so much more.

Not only that, they enlisted several Pinoy stars for the music video, ranging from icons, musicians, and content creators, namely: Kween Yasmin, Malupiton, Smugglaz, Shehyee, Alodia Gosiengfiao, Mimiyuuuh, Ben&Ben’s Pat Lasaten and Agnes Reoma, Maymay Entrata, Sassa Gurl, Jayat, Ghost Wrecker, and Meme herself, Vice Ganda.

“DUNGKA!” is an upbeat rave track from SB19’s much-awaited EP “[Simula at Wakas](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/941949/sb19-simula-at-wakas-ep-track-list/story/),” which dropped on Friday. The album also includes the comeback single, “[DAM](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/940260/david-licauco-joins-sb19-s-stell-ken-for-dam-challenge/story/)” from February.

The P-Pop Kings will kick off their Simula at Wakas World Tour with a t[wo-night concert](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/942163/sb19-announces-ticket-prices-for-simula-at-wakas-day-2-concert/story/) at the Philippine Arena in Bulacan on May 31 and June 1.

After the Bulacan concerts, SB19 will have their [world tour](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/935985/sb19-announces-simula-at-wakas-world-tour/story/) across 18 cities in Asia and the Pacific, the Middle East, and North America. **—Nika Roque/JCB, GMA Integrated News**

![Image 1: SB19 releases phenomenal finale of EP trilogy 'Simula at Wakas' alongside poignant music video for 'DUNGKA!' & 'Time'](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/crop=d:%5B0%2C1539%2C7789%2C3894%5D/resize=w:1920/pjpg=q:90/compress/MYZGnE4tSiegxL7nygUO)

Celebrating a journey marked by shared experience, invaluable wisdom, and artistic growth, **SB19** returns with the release of their third EP, **_Simula at Wakas_**—out on all digital music platforms worldwide via **Sony Music Entertainment**. Their highly anticipated body of work captures the band’s evolution as artists and individuals, honoring the past while stepping boldly into the future.

“It’s our way of saying thank you and showing how much we’ve evolved,” P-pop kings share in an official statement. “_Simula at Wakas_ encapsulates everything we’ve been through: the struggles, the growth, the milestones. We hope it speaks not only to those who’ve been with us from the start but also welcomes new listeners into our world.”

As the final installment in a trilogy that began with 2021’s **_pagsibol_** and 2023’s **_PAGTATAG!_**, _Simula at Wakas_ chronicles the Filipino pop group’s artistic and personal transformation while signaling a bold, forward-looking direction. The EP explores the universal themes of closure and renewal, portraying the life of an artist as they navigate fame, pressure, and identity. The band further shared personal anecdotes and reflections on their journey to _Simula at Wakas_ in the _**This is SB19**_ playlist on Spotify.

The P-pop trailblazers explain, “It’s both a celebration of our journey so far and a declaration of what’s to come. We’re the same group as when we started. It's just that we’ve matured, evolved, and grown into artists who are more confident in our voice and purpose.”

_Simula at Wakas_ showcases the 'DAM' hitmakers' captivating and universally relatable sound, all while remaining true to their values as human beings. From emotionally resonant lyrics to innovative, genre-bending soundscapes, the EP offers a meaningful experience that is sure to leave a lasting impression.

The release is written and produced by SB19 with their trusted pool of international and local collaborators, including **Xerxes Bakker**, **Alawn**, **August Rigo**, **Simon Servida**, and **Josue (RADKIDZ)**. The EP features the full creative involvement of all five members. SB19 admits that they took a hands-on approach in shaping every aspect of the project and were very deliberate in contributing not just musically but also creatively—from the narrative of each track to its visual interpretation, from the choreography to music videos.

“We held meetings almost every day to carefully discuss how each song would come together, from conceptualizing and message to planning how we could execute and promote the EP in ways we’ve never done before,” SB19 explains. “This is the first time after how many years that every member has been this hands-on. Everyone was involved in conceptualizing, producing, and writing the songs. But we also owe a lot to our collaborators who helped us push our ideas further and elevate the project on both the technical and creative sides.”

The envelope-pushing EP cements their position as one of the vital forces behind contemporary pop music in the Philippines and Southeast Asia for the last decade, providing a riveting insight into less explored paths and a thrilling outlook for future developments. _Simula at Wakas_ contains seven songs, including the now-viral single **'DAM'** alongside the focus tracks **'DUNGKA!'** and **'Time'**.

The anthemic ballad 'Time' essays the inevitability of time’s passing—an undeniable and unavoidable reality. As the lyrics go, “One day we’ll run out of time,” the song reveals a sobering reminder of life’s impermanence, yet one that inspires purpose and presence. “Hindi naman kami forever SB19,” acknowledges the five-piece act. “Nothing is permanent in this world, even from where we are at this point. Time will run out soon. All we can do is try our best and make the most out it.”

'DUNGKA!', another focus track, vaults SB19 back to their experimental phase: evangelizing pop music in unrecognizably exciting form and embracing maximalist production with rave and hyper-pop elements. It’s easily one of the biggest surprises of the EP, standing its ground as both a sonic rebel and revelation.

To complement the EP’s release, SB19 introduces the **DAM Tree**, an immersive public art installation, now open to the public in Bonifacio Global City (BGC) until 4 May. As part of the promotional campaign, fans can experience the world of **Simula at Wakas** through hanging parabolic sound domes where **A’TIN** first heard exclusive track previews from the EP. Beyond the immersive listening experience, visitors also get the chance to win exciting prizes, quickly becoming a hotspot for fan frenzy.

“A tree, by nature, reflects life’s different stages, starting from a seed, growing roots, eventually branching out and bearing,” the group explains. “That aligns with the message of 'DAM' and the EP as a whole: acknowledging where we began, embracing how we’ve evolved, and looking ahead to what’s next. The DAM Tree is not just a design; it’s an experience. We wanted people to feel connected to the music in a more immersive way. It’s our way of turning the emotions behind Simula at Wakas into something you can actually see and feel.”

Further solidifying this milestone, SB19 will kick off the [_**Simula at Wakas World Tour**_](https://www.bandwagon.asia/articles/sb19-sell-out-simula-at-wakas-world-tour-stops-in-record-time-announce-singapore-leg-in-august) with two landmark concerts at the iconic **Philippine Arena** on 31 May and 1 June, with the first one already sold out. The tour will span across major cities in Taiwan, the United States, Canada, Singapore, and the Middle East from June to October this year, with additional stops in Australia, Japan, and Hong Kong to be announced.

“We’ve been working on new arrangements for some of our songs, and we’re really excited for fans to hear them,” the group shares. “We’ll be performing tracks from our latest EP, _Simula at Wakas_, and we can’t wait to share the energy and emotion behind each song. Every performance has been thoughtfully prepared, and we’re really looking forward to seeing how our fans react to these new versions of our music. Each day will be a different experience!”

SB19’s ‘DUNGKA!’ Is a Joyful Portrait of Filipino Life—And a Sharp Middle Finger To Negativity
==============================================================================================

In a luminous swirl of street life, protest chants, and sticky-sweet nostalgia, _DUNGKA!_ captures the defiant heartbeat of a nation refusing to stand still

By [Dayne Aduna](https://vman-sea.com/author/dayne-aduna/ "Posts by Dayne Aduna")

April 26, 2025

[![Image 4: Facebook](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/facebook.svg)](https://www.addtoany.com/add_to/facebook?linkurl=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F&linkname=SB19%E2%80%99s%20%26%238216%3BDUNGKA%21%26%238217%3B%20Is%20a%20Joyful%20Portrait%20of%20Filipino%20Life%E2%80%94And%20a%20Sharp%20Middle%20Finger%20To%20Negativity "Facebook")[![Image 5: Instagram](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/instagram.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Instagram")[![Image 6: X](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/x.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "X")[![Image 7: Email](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/email.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Email")[![Image 8: Copy Link](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/link.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Copy Link")

  ![Image 9: sb19 DUNGKA!](https://b3720787.smushcdn.com/3720787/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/sb19-dungka-banner.webp?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

A soundtrack for defiance and joy
---------------------------------

It was only fitting that SB19—the luminary architects of P-pop’s current renaissance—graced the cover of our [Spring 2025 issue](https://vman-sea.com/on-the-cover/sb19-the-brotherhood-behind-the-music-and-why-theyre-stronger-than-ever/). Even then, they seemed poised on the brink of another breakthrough, and with the release of the _DUNGKA!_ music video, they have, once again, pushed beyond the expected.

_DUNGKA!_ is a six-minute exhale of Filipino life: vivid, messy, and magnetic. The music video stitches together a tapestry of the archipelago’s pulse—street basketball courts alive with sweaty, frenetic games; vendors hawking _kwek-kwek_ and _isaw_; karaoke sessions conducted in cracked plastic chairs; Zumba in parking lots; children hopping between chalk squares in 10-20; rally banners flapping against concrete and sky. Election campaigns roar in the background, as much a fixture of the landscape as the sunset-lit jeepneys rattling down narrow streets. Every frame hums with the particular, chaotic beauty of ordinary days in the Philippines.

And threaded through it all, like a live wire: SB19, effortless in their command, moving not above the scenes, but through them.

_ALSO READ: [FELIP’s Meteoric Rise](https://vman-sea.com/arts-culture/music/felips-meteoric-rise/)_

Staying stubbornly, brilliantly local
-------------------------------------

Musically, _DUNGKA!_— produced by Pablo and his brother Josue under their RadKidz moniker—is a rave-fueled masterstroke. Over a pounding beat, Pablo and Josh trade bold rap verses, their delivery swaggering and infectious. Pablo’s wordplay turns the everyday Filipino phrase “_doon ka_” (“go over there”) into a playful, defiant refrain—a winking incantation to repel bad vibes, dead weight, and unwanted forces.

Advertisement

The effect is both jubilant and cutting. If the song is an invitation to join the revelry, it is also a gatekeeping spell: only those who belong, who understand, may stay.

      ![Image 10: sb19](https://b3720787.smushcdn.com/3720787/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/VMAN-SB19-2.jpg?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

on josh, pablo, ken, and stell:  
all clothing _**tod’s**_ / jewelry _**bvlgari**_

—

on justin:

all clothing _**brunello cucinelli**_ / jewelry _**bvlgari**_

Yet beyond its aesthetic bravado and sonic innovation, _DUNGKA!_ is significant because it refuses to dilute itself. It is deeply and stubbornly local, packed with references that demand fluency, but offered generously enough to welcome newcomers. It is a pop star flex, but also an archival act: a documentation of how Filipinos live, love, eat, protest, and endure.

In an era when many artists aspire to cross borders by sanding down their cultural particularities, SB19 does the opposite. They dig deeper. And somehow, in doing so, they make their music—and their movement—feel not just national, but planetary.

Advertisement

After all, specificity is what makes universality possible. In the chaotic beauty of _DUNGKA!_, SB19 reminds us that the more vividly you show your own world, the more the world will want to see.

14.content:
SB19 didn’t just show up to sing and dance. They came to shake the room, throw a giant party, sprinkle in life lessons, and leave us thinking about it for days. “Dungka” is not just a song or a video. It is a whole moment in pop culture. If you have seen it, you know. If you have not, well, you are seriously missing out.

Here are five reasons why fans can’t stop calling this MV iconic.

**1\. It is a Hidden Treasure Chest of Meaning**

At first glance, “Dungka” looks like a chaotic street party. Balloons everywhere. Crazy dance battles. Zumba in the parking lot. But fans quickly caught on that every scene means something. “Dungka” is slangy for “doon ka,” which means “go there” or “go away” in Tagalog, and in Hiligaynon, it can also mean “to arrive at port.” It is all about movement, journeys, and facing where life takes you.

Scenes like Ghost Wrecker gobbling down a crab are not just funny. That is a jab at “crab mentality,” where people pull each other down instead of lifting each other up. Zumba classes and the winks at breaking gender roles. Rap battles? That is the spirit of Filipino street smarts, creativity, and fighting through words instead of fists.

Every colorful moment hits you with something deeper if you look just a little closer.

**2\. They Took Shots at Society in the Most Fun Way Possible**

Most songs that talk about problems tend to get really heavy. But SB19 managed to clap back at all the negativity like judgment, stereotyping, and cancel culture without making it feel like homework. It is fun, but the message is loud and clear. Society loves to judge, but you do not have to live your life by their rules.

Instead of preaching, they are like that one friend who jokes about everything but secretly gives the best advice when you are about to make a dumb life choice.

**3\. The Guest List Was a Whole Party by Itself**

Let us get this straight. SB19 did not just invite random people. They brought out legends, icons, and people who each represent something beautiful about Filipino culture. And they showed up in this order:

*   [Ghost Wrecker](https://www.facebook.com/ghostwrecker28/) — gaming legend
*   [Kween Yasmin](https://www.facebook.com/www.facebookyasminasistido.090/) — hilarious and vibrant online personality
*   [Malupiton](https://www.facebook.com/borgerkasakenboy/) — master of witty content
*   [Smugglaz](https://www.facebook.com/Smugglaz187MOB/) — a rap king
*   [Shehyee](https://www.facebook.com/shehyee/) — another rap champ
*   [Alodia Gosiengfiao](https://www.facebook.com/AlodiaGosiengfiao/) — queen of cosplay
*   [Mimiyuuuh](https://www.facebook.com/mimiyuuuh/) — fashionista and comedian rolled into one
*   [Pat Lasaten](https://www.instagram.com/patlasaten/?hl=en) — from Ben&Ben, musical genius
*   [Agnes Reoma](https://www.instagram.com/agnesreoma/?hl=en) — also from Ben&Ben, making magic on the bass
*   [Maymay Entrata](https://www.instagram.com/maymay/?hl=en) — actress, model, and overall star
*   [Sassa Gurl](https://www.facebook.com/Sassagurl/) — queen of online humor and sass
*   [Jayat](https://www.facebook.com/JayatGamingTV/) — fresh face from the rap battle scene
*   [Vice Ganda](https://www.instagram.com/praybeytbenjamin/?hl=en) — comedian royalty and LGBTQ+ icon

Each guest was not just there to pose for the camera. They were woven into the story. It felt like a real community, a huge melting pot of different talents and personalities. Just like the Philippines itself.

**4\. It Was the Most Filipino Thing Ever**

No glammed-up skyscrapers. No rented supercars. No trying to look international. “Dungka” was all about us. The streets, the games, the music, the crazy, happy, everyday life of being Pinoy.

There were street courts, carinderia scenes, fliptop battles, Zumba sessions, messy barkadahan moments, and yes, even the karaoke we all know and love. SB19 showed that being Filipino is already world-class. No filters needed.

**5\. It Gave the Biggest, Sassiest Middle Finger to Negativity**

At the heart of everything, “Dungka” tells you this. Life is tough. People will judge you, laugh at you, and try to pull you down. But who cares? Go live your life anyway. Wear what you want. Dance how you feel. Be loud. Be soft. Be whoever the heck you want to be.

That is the real magic of this MV. It was not about pretending everything is perfect. It was about dancing through the mess and living despite the critics. Fans said it felt like being handed a mic and told, “Your voice matters too. Now go sing your heart out.”

Dungka is not just a music video. It is a love letter to everyone who has ever been judged, doubted, or told to shrink themselves. SB19 basically said, “Nah. You are bigger than that. Let us celebrate.”

And honestly? We are so here for it.
